::: {.solutions}

Marks: **(M1)** method, **(A1)** accuracy, **(B1)** independent. Total **46**.

Two habits to check: before differentiating, did they **rewrite as powers of $x$** (surds and fractions become
$x^{p}$)? When they classify a stationary point or an increasing/decreasing region, did they justify with the
**sign** of $f'$ or $f''$ — and, for fractional powers, remember that $x^{-1/3}<0$ when $x<0$?

---

# Section A — Differentiate

## Question 1 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac92\sqrt{x}+\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{x}}$; value $7$ at $x=1$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Split into powers first:* $y=3x^{3/2}-5x^{-1/2}$ **(M1)**. Then
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\tfrac92x^{1/2}+\tfrac52x^{-1/2}$ **(A1)**. At $x=1$: $\tfrac92+\tfrac52=7$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 2 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$f''(4)=1$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

$f(x)=2x^{3/2}+8x^{-1}$, so $f'(x)=3x^{1/2}-8x^{-2}$ **(M1)** and $f''(x)=\tfrac32x^{-1/2}+16x^{-3}$ **(A1)**. At
$x=4$: $\tfrac32\cdot\tfrac12+16\cdot\tfrac{1}{64}=\tfrac34+\tfrac14=1$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section B — Stationary points & max/min

## Question 3 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**Maximum $(-1,12)$; minimum $(2,-15)$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Set $y'=0$.* $y'=6x^2-6x-12=6(x-2)(x+1)=0\Rightarrow x=-1,\,2$ **(M1 A1)**. *Classify with $y''=12x-6$:* at
$x=-1$, $y''=-18<0$ → **maximum**, $y=12$; at $x=2$, $y''=18>0$ → **minimum**, $y=-15$ **(A1 A1)**.
:::

## Question 4 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$p=4$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Complete the square: the minimum of $x^2+px+7$ is $7-\dfrac{p^2}{4}$* **(M1)**. Set this equal to $3$:
$7-\dfrac{p^2}{4}=3\Rightarrow p^2=16$ **(A1)**, so the positive value is $p=4$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 5 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**Maximum area $32$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*By symmetry the rectangle spans $-x$ to $x$, with height $12-x^2$, so its area is* $A=2x(12-x^2)=24x-2x^3$
**(M1 A1)**. *Maximise:* $A'=24-6x^2=0\Rightarrow x=2$ (taking $x>0$) **(A1)**. Then
$A=2(2)(12-4)=4\cdot8=32$ **(A1)**. *(Since $A''=-12x<0$ at $x=2$, it is a maximum.)*
:::

# Section C — Increasing / decreasing

## Question 6 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x<-1$ or $x>3$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Increasing means $f'>0$.* $y'=3x^2-6x-9=3(x-3)(x+1)$ **(M1 A1)**. This upward parabola is positive **outside**
its roots, so $x<-1$ or $x>3$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 7 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$0<x<2$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Write in powers and differentiate:* $f(x)=x^{5/3}-5x^{2/3}$, so
$f'(x)=\tfrac53x^{2/3}-\tfrac{10}{3}x^{-1/3}=\tfrac53x^{-1/3}(x-2)$ **(M1 A1)**. *For $x>0$, $x^{-1/3}>0$, so
$f'<0$ exactly when $x-2<0$; for $x<0$ the factor $x^{-1/3}<0$ makes $f'>0$.* Hence $f$ decreases on
$0<x<2$ **(A1)**.
:::

# Section D — Parameters, tangents, normals & roots

## Question 8 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**Gradient $=a^2-10a+16$; least value $-9$ (at $a=5$).** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Differentiate in $x$ (product rule):* $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(x-a)^2+(x+1)\cdot2(x-a)$ **(M1)**. *Put $x=2$:*
$(2-a)^2+3\cdot2(2-a)=(2-a)^2+6(2-a)=a^2-10a+16$ **(A1)**. *This is an upward parabola in $a$; complete the
square:* $=(a-5)^2-9$ **(A1)**, so the least gradient is $-9$, at $a=5$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 9 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$Q=\left(0,\tfrac52\right)$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x$, so the tangent gradient at $(1,2)$ is $2$ and the **normal** gradient is $-\tfrac12$
**(M1)**. Normal: $y-2=-\tfrac12(x-1)$ **(A1)**. At $x=0$, $y=2+\tfrac12=\tfrac52$, so $Q=\left(0,\tfrac52\right)$
**(A1)**.
:::

## Question 10 **[4]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$3$ real roots.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1 A1)**

*Find the turning points.* $y'=3x^2-3=0\Rightarrow x=\pm1$ **(M1)**. *Evaluate $y$ there:* $y(-1)=-1+3+1=3$
(local max) and $y(1)=1-3+1=-1$ (local min) **(A1 A1)**. *A cubic runs from $-\infty$ to $+\infty$; since the
local max is positive and the local min is negative, the curve crosses the axis three times* → **3** real roots
**(A1)**.
:::

## Question 11 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$2$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*The gradient function is $y'=3x^2-6x+5$; minimise it (it is itself a quadratic).* Complete the square:
$3(x-1)^2+2$ **(M1 A1)**. Its least value is $2$, at $x=1$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 12 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$x=2$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*A point of inflection occurs where $y''=0$ (and changes sign).* $y'=3x^2-12x+9$, $y''=6x-12$ **(M1 A1)**.
$y''=0\Rightarrow x=2$; since $y''$ changes from negative to positive there, it is a genuine inflection **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 13 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$y=\tfrac14x+1$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$, so at $x=4$ the gradient is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ **(M1)**. The point is $(4,2)$.
Tangent: $y-2=\tfrac14(x-4)$ **(A1)**, i.e. $y=\tfrac14x+1$ **(A1)**.
:::

## Question 14 **[3]**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Answer
**$256$.** &nbsp; **(M1 A1 A1)**

*Substitute the constraint $y=12-x$ to get one variable:* maximise $f(x)=x^2(12-x)=12x^2-x^3$ **(M1)**.
$f'(x)=24x-3x^2=3x(8-x)=0\Rightarrow x=8$ (taking $x>0$) **(A1)**. Then $y=4$ and $x^2y=64\cdot4=256$ **(A1)**.
:::
